extracted.intended_audience: health researchers, clinical investigators, journal editors, peer reviewers and authors preparing or evaluating health research reports
extracted.subtask_description: A curated library and index of reporting guidelines for health research, mapping common study types (randomised trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, protocols, diagnostic/prognostic studies, qualitative research, animal studies, economic evaluations, quality improvement, clinical practice guidelines, case reports, etc.) to their recommended reporting statements (e.g., CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, SPIRIT, STARD, TRIPOD, ARRIVE, SQUIRE, CHEERS, AGREE, RIGHT, CARE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomised trials — CONSORT (Extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: CONSORT (Preferred Reporting Items for Randomised Trials). Extensions for various randomised trial designs are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CONSORT statement and the relevant CONSORT extension appropriate to the trial design (e.g., cluster, crossover, non-pharmacologic, pragmatic, abstracts); see the CONSORT 2010 statement and its extension checklists and explanation/elaboration documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational studies — STROBE (Extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: STROBE (Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology) and its extensions for different observational study types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the STROBE checklist items appropriate to the observational design (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) and consult any extensions for specialty areas or specific data sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic reviews — PRISMA (Extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) and extensions for different types of evidence syntheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the PRISMA checklist appropriate to the review type (e.g., network meta-analyses, scoping reviews) and consult PRISMA explanation and elaboration resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study protocols — SPIRIT / PRISMA-P
rubrics_metrics.description: SPIRIT (Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials) and PRISMA-P (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic review and Meta-Analysis Protocols) for protocol reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report protocols using SPIRIT for clinical trial protocols and PRISMA-P for systematic review protocols, including required items for transparency and prospective registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic / prognostic studies — STARD / TRIPOD
rubrics_metrics.description: STARD (Standards for Reporting of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies) and TRIPOD (Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis Or Diagnosis) for diagnostic and prognostic research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use STARD checklists for diagnostic accuracy studies and TRIPOD for development/validation of prediction models, following the itemized reporting recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case reports — CARE (Extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: CARE (CAse REport) guidelines and extensions for reporting individual clinical case reports and series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the CARE checklist to ensure key clinical information, diagnostic assessment, therapeutic intervention, follow-up and patient perspective are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical practice guidelines — AGREE / RIGHT
rubrics_metrics.description: AGREE (Appraisal of Guidelines for Research & Evaluation) reporting checklist and the RIGHT (Reporting Items for practice Guidelines in HealThcare) statement for guideline development and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AGREE/RIGHT items to report guideline scope, stakeholder involvement, evidence synthesis, recommendations, and editorial independence for transparent guideline reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative research — SRQR / COREQ
rubrics_metrics.description: SRQR (Standards for Reporting Qualitative Research) and COREQ (Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research) checklists for qualitative studies (e.g., interviews, focus groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report qualitative study context, sampling, data collection, analysis, researcher reflexivity and data saturation using SRQR/COREQ items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal (pre-clinical) studies — ARRIVE
rubrics_metrics.description: ARRIVE (Animal Research: Reporting of In Vivo Experiments) guidelines for reporting animal research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include key details on experimental animals, housing, husbandry, experimental procedures, statistical methods, and ethical approvals per ARRIVE to improve reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality improvement studies — SQUIRE
rubrics_metrics.description: SQUIRE (Standards for Quality Improvement Reporting Excellence) reporting guidelines for quality improvement studies and initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe problem context, intervention details, measures, study of the intervention, analysis, and interpretation according to SQUIRE items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic evaluations — CHEERS
rubrics_metrics.description: CHEERS (Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards) statement for reporting economic evaluation studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report study perspective, comparators, time horizon, costs, outcomes, modelling methods, sensitivity analyses and relevance to decision makers following CHEERS items.
